articles.title: "We felt that fans were getting a bit desensitised to the violence" Gears of War: E-Day devs made a "big investment" in gore, and weirdly, it works
articles.summary: Buoyed by some commendatory early reviews and fantastic initial player numbers, Gears of War: E-Day has found a solid audience a weekend before general release. And a large part of its appeal is the combat; I noted in my review I think it's the tightest Gears has ever been, augmented by some…
body: And it turns out there's a lot more intricate thought behind this eruption of violence than perhaps people realise, as I discovered in an interview with Coalition studio art director Aryan Hanbeck, brand director Nicole Fawcett, and creative director Matt Searcy.

"Think about getting a headshot, right, a really good headshot," says Hanbeck. "A lot of work goes into that moment, into what happens on the screen when you take a headshot. There's an audio component to that, too, as well as all the effects - how high the blood spurts go, how much mist we leave behind, what the body does afterwards… So, it's not just the weapon itself, it's what you see and hear when you do what it's supposed to do, or when you get up close and you melee with [your Lancer or Breechshot] or execute an enemy, which is really cool."
"And there's a big investment in gore in this game," adds Searcy. "That's a huge aspect of [what makes combat so satisfying]."
points: Buoyed by some commendatory early reviews and fantastic initial player numbers, Gears of War: E-Day has found a solid audience a weekend before general release.
"Think about getting a headshot, right, a really good headshot," says Hanbeck.
"A lot of work goes into that moment, into what happens on the screen when you take a headshot.
"And there's a big investment in gore in this game," adds Searcy.

articles.title: 45 Years Ago, a Failed Lord of the Rings Movie Became a Film That Transcended Fantasy
articles.summary: In the late 15th century, a man named Thomas Malory, whose identity is still debated by scholars, wrote Le Morte d’Arthur, a compilation of legends, chivalric poems, and folklore related to King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table.
body: As some critics pointed out over the years, Boorman’s epic can throw off spectators with its disjointed flow and weird dialogue. The characters have also been criticized for being inconsistent due to the frequent time jumps in the story, while the plot has been accused of lacking dramatic intensity. However, this is all a result of design rather than incompetence. Excalibur feels more like seeing a stage play than a movie. Every scene is a set piece, a tableau where a fragment of the fairy Arthurian world comes to life. The movie isn’t trying to show a story in the traditional sense. Rather, it attempts something that few works of visual media succeeded at: telling a myth.

Just like myths carry their meaningful symbolism through the ages thanks to powerful images, so Boorman’s ambitious attempt to adapt King Arthur’s tale lives on through the enduring strength of its visuals.

The 2015 film stars Emily Blunt as principled FBI agent Kate Macer, who is enlisted by the U.S. government to help capture a Mexican drug cartel leader with the aid of CIA agent Matt Graver (Josh Brolin) and former Mexican prosecutor turned assassin Alejandro Gillick (Benicio del Toro). articles.title: Love and Deepspace Devs Issue Warning to Players After Deadly Drink Recipes Go Viral
articles.summary: The official social media account for the popular RPG-dating sim Love and Deepspace issued a warning to players after announcing some fictional cocktails with potentially disastrous real-world consequences if actually consumed.
body: On September 28, Love and Deepspace revealed five ‘Shimmering Blend’ cocktail recipes as part of an in-game event, each themed around one of the game’s dashing romanceable characters. While they’re pretty to look at, you shouldn’t actually make some of these, as they include garnishes that are poisonous to humans.
For example, one of these drinks is made of pomegranate juice, with a garnish of cinnamon and datura. Another features sweet peach juice with a flame lily garnish and gelatin sheets.

There’s nothing wrong with peach and pomegranate juice, but these floral garnishes are making some players anxious that a fan might actually try to out the recipes themselves. Datura is a highly poisonous plant and is considered psychoactive; when consumed, it produces side effects like delirium, fever, tachychardia, and hallucinations.

Flame Lilies are also dangerous, as all parts of the plant contain a chemical called colchicine; while it’s used for medicinal purposes, it can be lethal, causing symptoms like fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and even hypovolemic shock, which causes the loss of lethal amounts of blood and bodily fluids.

articles.title: Dimension 20 Best Season to Start? 6 Campaigns to Get Into Dropout’s D&D Show
articles.summary: After performing for nearly 20,000 fans at a sold-out Madison Square Garden in January 2025, Dimension 20 cemented its status as one of the internet’s most popular tabletop live-play shows.
body: That may sound like a lot, but that’s only because it is. Getting into any long-running actual-play series requires the sort of commitment usually reserved for sprawling anime franchises. Even D20’s longer campaigns are snack-sized compared to a single season of Critical Role, but you could still spend anywhere from five to 60 hours completing one story.
It’s natural to wonder where you should begin, particularly because D20’s original season is also the beginning of its longest-running campaign.

This guide is meant to help interested newcomers choose where to start. Not every D20 campaign is created equal, and even devoted fans commonly bounce off entire seasons. These six campaigns offer some of the best possible starting points, depending on exactly what you’re looking for.
Dimension 20 ’s second season remains one of its most accessible. It has a simple hook, runs for only six episodes, and is available to watch in full for free through D20’s official YouTube channel.

articles.title: Steam Horror Game Turns PS1-Era Graphics Into Backrooms-Style Nightmare Fuel
articles.summary: There is something uniquely unsettling about empty video game spaces. Blown wide open in the wake of Backrooms, the concept of liminal horror has seeped out from internet forums and chat rooms to become a subculture all its own.
body: It’s a feeling written into the code of some of the greatest PS1 games ever made, from Tomb Raider to Metal Gear Solid. Often born from the limited memory and technical constraints of mid-’90s consoles, such games inadvertently — or deliberately if you’re Silent Hill — turned empty digital spaces into breeding grounds for a sense of unease. This idea would be taken to an even stranger extreme long after the PS1 became a legacy system, thanks to Bryce Bucher’s surreal 2020 horror adventure Fatum Betula. Almost six years after release, it remains one of the clearest examples of how PlayStation-era 3D environments can transform even the emptiest spaces into something deeply unsettling.

articles.title: Capcom Announces Plans to Transform the RE Engine Into an AI-Generation Game Engine — ‘Our Goal Is a Future Where We Create Games Together With AI’
articles.summary: Resident Evil and Street Fighter developer Capcom revealed some big changes coming to its RE Engine, which they plan to incrementally improve and transform into an "AI-generation game engine." On October 2, Capcom held its own tech conference, called ‘Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026.’ One of the…
body: As reported by Japanese news outlet GameBiz, Ishida mentioned three major issues that Capcom is currently experiencing when it comes to game development: First, games are now so massive that simple processes have become extremely time-consuming; increased numbers of staff mean an engine is needed that’s easy for everyone to use; and finally, “successfully integrating AI technology into development workflows has become an essential condition for streamlining future development.”

GameBiz’s report confirmed that REX was created to help solve these problems by improving the efficiency of game development, game performance, tools, quality assurance, etc. Capcom felt that, rather than creating a brand-new engine from scratch, gradually adding these improvements over time is the best way to help evolve the RE Engine to the next generation.

We won’t get into the weeds of all the specific improvements included in the REX program, but Capcom is making at least some of them open-source for the purpose of training AI. Most interestingly, AI plays into Capcom’s larger, long-term goal of turning the RE Engine into an “AI-generation game engine” using its REX improvements.

articles.summary: Hello and welcome back to our regular feature where we write a little about the games we've been playing. This week, Bertie's witcher skills are a bit rusty; Dom goes through the Gears; Kelsey enjoys a horror game that feels just like home; and Chris does an incredible impression of a butler that…
body: And don't forget we have an entire dusty archive of previous What We've Been Playings, just in case you don't trust your memory any more and want to check which games you've played and see what you thought of them.

It's weird returning to a game I think I know really well only to discover I don't really know it that well any more at all. The familiarity slowly dribbles back and broad strokes of the game I can of course remember, but that muscle memory that was once so readily there has gone. I bumbled around like an idiot in The Witcher 3 for a couple of hours when revisiting it for the Remastered release this week. I felt like Roach stranded on a rooftop.

I compared the game a lot to The Blood of Dawnwalker while I played, too, which isn't a surprise given how similar they are, and in how they're directed by the same person, Konrad Tomaszkiewicz (and made by many of the same people). And stood side by side, The Witcher 3 holds up remarkably well, which is impressive given that it's now 11 years old.

articles.title: End Of Abyss Patch Fixes Most Of My Complaints Just One Day After Launch
articles.summary: I spent a few days playing Section 9 Interactive's creepy metroidvania and writing my End of Abyss review, and ultimately concluded it was a fun but inconsistent experience hindered by a few particular issues.
body: If you missed the review, my main concern was how the in-game map would sometimes share incorrect information, like telling me a door was locked when I had unlocked it, or failing to signify when I'd found the key to a particular door. In a metroidvania, this means a whole lot. End of Abyss is a game about exploration, including lots of backtracking via roundabout paths, so when I'd plan long treks across the world based on a faulty map, it was really frustrating to find out too late that I'd essentially been lied to.

But a patch has fixed that, among other problems, and it presents an uncommon issue for me. My review only went out two days ago. The game only launched yesterday. Now much of my review is already outdated. In this era of live-service games and post-launch updates, it's common for games to change shape over time, but for End of Abyss's patch to fix many of its lesser parts essentially right after the deadline isn't normally how it goes.

articles.title: Former NFL Coach Mike Tomlin Is a Hardcore Minecraft Player, Reveals City He Took 12 Years to Build
articles.summary: Former NFL coach Mike Tomlin spent 19 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers and won Super Bowl LXIII, and now he's added another major accomplishment to his resume: becoming a Minecraft YouTuber.
body: The former coach gave football fans a little something different when he launched his new YouTube channel earlier this week. With a profile picture taken in front of NBC's Football Night in America logo, watchers probably weren't expecting Tomlin's first upload to see him confess how his love for architecture and family led him to work on a Minecraft city he spent 12 years building.

"You know, 12 or 13 years ago, when my kids were in middle school, they'd be in their room all weekend and have friends over. They were obsessed with playing this game, Minecraft, that I knew nothing about," he explained as his son and channel operator, Dino, sat in the background. "I got interested because I just was mesmerized by what could occupy their attention for such large periods of time."

He admitted he lacked the "stick control" to handle something like Minecraft's Survival mode but still managed to find enjoyment in Creative Mode. That's where Mojang's systems really started to click.

articles.title: GTA 6 Screenshot Suggests It Won’t Be Shy About Movie References
articles.summary: A new screenshot from Grand Theft Auto 6 has arrived, and fans immediately noticed that it appears to be referencing the iconic opening scene from Quentin Tarantino's 1994 crime movie Pulp Fiction. The image was shared by Love magazine on Instagram.
body: In Pulp Fiction, Tim Roth and Amanda Plummer's characters, Pumpkin and Honey Bunny, go on to rob the diner, and given that Lucia and Jason are criminals as well, it's not a stretch to think that could happen in GTA 6. Maybe they're just enjoying breakfast, but that seems unlikely given the image clearly shows both gripping their pistols, with Lucia seemingly ready to fill the empty duffel bag next to her with cash and other valuables.

GTA 6 tells a Bonnie and Clyde-style story of two lovers who are also criminals. Things did not end well for them, and many are speculating as to how GTA 6's story could wrap up for both Lucia and Jason. It also wouldn't be surprising to see GTA 6 reference Pulp Fiction given how GTA games in the past have featured very overt references to movies, like how Vice City had Scarface references and GTA 5 had nods to Heat.

"We wanted both protagonists to be vulnerable, tough, flawed, right sometimes, wrong sometimes, able to learn from each other,”GTA 6 writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern told Love magazine. “That’s what we felt made them authentic, and a great team.”

articles.title: GTA 6 Should “Blaze A Trail” To More Expensive Games, Dev Says
articles.summary: Rockstar's GTA 6 is priced at $80 for its standard edition. Another voice has come forward to say they hope other teams follow suit and charge more for new games to help the industry at a time when developers are closing up shop, cancelling games, and laying off developers on a regular basis.
body: Martin Klima, the co-founder of Kingdom Come developer Warhorse, told PC Gamer that raising unit prices would "help a lot," but "everybody's scared to death" to do it.

"Now, hopefully, GTA will blaze the trail, and it will allow us to increase the cost," he said, adding that Rockstar and Take-Two are among the only companies who can "afford, or who can dare" to raise prices in this way.
He added that price increases for new games are "long overdue and also necessary for this business to survive."

Take-Two was among the first big publishers to drive prices up from $60 to $70, kicking this off with NBA 2K21 in 2020. Numerous other publishers followed suit, and now $70 is the norm. Defending the price increase, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick said production costs increased by 300%.

articles.title: GTA 6 Takes The Ridiculous World We Live In And Turns It Up To 11
articles.summary: Video games are usually a few steps removed from reality, but with Grand Theft Auto 6, developer Rockstar Games aims to reflect and amplify the current state of the world with an "over the top" experience.
body: "If you are going to put all this effort into creating a version of today’s world, it has to be more over the top, more insane, more in your face," senior VP of narrative Rupert Humphries said to Love Magazine. "Otherwise, you could just go outside and live in the real world."

Humphries also described the world of GTA 6 as "a pressure cooker for all kinds of insanity," as the protagonists, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, are polar opposites. Game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern described Lucina as an ambitious go-getter who'll do anything to get the life she dreams of, while Jason is bound by life's circumstances. "We wanted both protagonists to be vulnerable, tough, flawed, right sometimes, wrong sometimes, able to learn from each other," Gauvey-Kern said.

body: "The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered’s greatest asset isn’t that it adds anything the original sorely lacked, but rather that it removes some of the biggest roadblocks to fun the 1.0 version was saddled with. Combat is more challenging but also easier to enjoy, movement is quicker and less irritating, and revised skill trees allow for more freedom. Even if it doesn’t manage to fix some of the technical issues (plus I’m sure there are some bugs waiting for me to encounter them that haven’t reared their ugly heads yet), it manages to make this classic RPG more enjoyable in 2026, and that’s worth yet another ride down its well-trodded roads."

body: A surprise to be sure - and a welcome one. Out of the blue, Sony has released QSSR - Quick Spectral Super Resolution - a refactoring of PS5 Pro's PSSR for the standard PlayStation 5. In this video, Rich and Oliver share their initial thoughts on the technology. We've got image quality comparisons from Marvel's Wolverine, we've got early performance testing from a PS5 dev kit, comparisons with PSSR and much more.

videos.title: I Can't Believe A Silly Star Wars Racing Roguelite Is One Of My Favorite Games This Year - Review
videos.summary: I never would have guessed that putting roguelike elements into a racer would create a winning formula.
body: I felt such a sense of whiplash jumping into Star Wars Galactic Racer from Zero Company. Unlike Zero Company--and plenty of the other Star Wars games we've gotten in recent years, like Survivor and Squadrons--Galactic Racer isn't trying to emulate the science-fantasy drama that defines the majority of the Star Wars movies and other assorted fiction.

videos.title: World of Tanks Modern Armor - Steel Asylum Trailer | PS5 & PS4 Games
videos.summary: Beware, Commander: the battlefield has descended into madness.
body: Step into Steel Asylum, the latest season of World of Tanks Modern Armor, and face 100 Stages packed with rewards worthy of those brave enough to confront the unknown. Earn Gold, War Chests, Premium Account time, Premium tanks, and more as you fight your way through a season where fear lurks around every corner.

Unlock the Season Pass and make your escape with the VCC-80/60, an Escalation Era Light Tank built to strike from the shadows and keep enemies guessing. Looking for an even greater advantage? The Ultimate Season Pass immediately grants you the Serpente — a deadly Tier IX medium tank ready to spread panic across the battlefield — and Desmond "Doc" Rose, a 3D Hero Commander whose unsettling expertise may be exactly what you need to survive the chaos ahead.
